reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a periodic rectangular pulse train with a fixed period of 48 points, as confirmed by the metadata and consistent spacing across all candidates. Each cycle consists of a near-instantaneous rise from baseline (robust standardized value ≈ 0.0) to a plateau at amplitude ≈ 2.47 (90th-percentile amplitude), held for ~13–15 points, followed by an equally sharp drop back to baseline. The plateau exhibits minimal roughness (MAD = 0.0 in catalog) and negligible curvature or slope—except candidate 1, which shows a slight negative slope (−0.017 per point) over its 3-cycle span, likely due to minor drift or quantization artifact rather than true trend, since other 3-cycle candidates (candidate 2) show zero slope. Baseline is stable at 0.0 across all segments; no long-term trend is present. Noise is effectively absent: all transitions are clean, vertical edges with no jitter, and plateaus are flat within plotting resolution. Peak morphology is square-like with near-vertical edges; troughs are flat baselines. Acceptable variation includes minor plateau waviness (e.g., candidate 3’s 5-cycle segment shows gentle undulations on top of the plateau, possibly due to residual high-frequency components or normalization artifacts), and very slight timing jitter (<1 point) in edge placement across cycles. No candidate shows irregular cycle length, missing pulses, or partial pulses—indicating high stability. The pattern is deterministic and highly reproducible across non-overlapping intervals, supporting its use as a robust normal template.

reference_profiles.description: Single-cycle (48-point) rectangular pulse: clean step up at index 8, flat plateau from 9–21 (~13 pts), sharp drop at 22 back to baseline. Perfectly flat baseline and plateau; zero slope, zero roughness. Ideal minimal representation of the motif.

Three-cycle segment showing three identical pulses spaced evenly (≈48 pts apart). Plateau has barely perceptible downward tilt (slope −0.017), visible as a slight sag over 144 points. Otherwise matches candidate 0 in shape, timing, and amplitude. Likely reflects minor global drift in the source window, not local anomaly.

Three-cycle segment identical in pulse shape and timing to candidate 0, with perfectly flat plateaus and zero slope. Serves as high-fidelity replication of candidate 0 at longer duration; confirms stability across non-adjacent windows.

Five-cycle segment showing five clean pulses. Plateaus exhibit subtle high-frequency ripple (small undulations), possibly due to residual signal or robust standardization artifacts, but amplitude, period, and edge sharpness remain consistent. No drift; baseline remains at 0.0. Most informative for assessing multi-cycle consistency.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 0 for single-cycle query matching (e.g., short windows or isolated anomalies); use reference 2 when comparing against 3-cycle queries requiring highest fidelity; use reference 3 for long-window queries (>200 pts) to assess multi-cycle coherence; treat reference 1 as secondary for 3-cycle analysis if slight drift is expected—but verify against reference 2 first. When query morphology shows plateau slope or ripple, compare against reference 1 (for slope) or 3 (for ripple) before flagging as anomalous.
